text:
The phrase is the intent element of common-law burglary: unlawfully entering a building or dwelling with the intent to commit a felony inside. The felony doesn't have to be carried out, but the intent must exist at the moment of entry, and many modern statutes widen it to any crime, including theft. The team note describes a contingent remainder, which is a property-law concept and doesn't fit this phrase, so I'm not changing my answer.

CONFIDENCE: 80
